## 2. YouTube description (the first two lines are the hook shown before “more”)

### 2.1 English (main) — 3047 characters (limit 5000)

```text
Lost count in the middle of a hundred-cell differential? There is a better way to keep the tally.
Where to count on the film, five cell types, and a one-tap counter in LabGuide.

In this video:
• Where to count on a stained blood film under the oil objective: the monolayer, where red cells touch but do not overlap, and how to move field by field without counting a cell twice.
• Segmented and band neutrophils, eosinophil, basophil, lymphocyte and monocyte, as schematic illustrations drawn by LabGuide on one scale (not micrographs).
• The tally in LabGuide on real app screens: one big button per cell class, 100 or 200 cells with a stop at the target, Microscope mode, percentages and absolute counts, saving the result.

Chapters
0:00 Where to count on the film
0:15 The cell types
0:44 Move along the film, tap per cell
1:04 Stop at the target, Microscope mode
1:21 Percent, absolute counts, ranges
1:40 Save or copy the result

What LabGuide does today:
• One big button per cell class (segmented and band neutrophils, lymphocyte, monocyte, eosinophil, basophil, other): a tap adds one, a long press takes one away.
• You choose 100 or 200 cells; at the target counting stops and an extra tap is not added.
• Microscope mode: large screen zones so your eyes can stay on the eyepiece, with sound and vibration cues where your phone supports and allows them.
• Percentages are computed by the app; enter the WBC and absolute counts appear next to them.
• Save the result on your device or copy it as text. LabGuide has no PDF export for this counter.

Good to know:
• The tally in the video is an illustrative example, not a typical or normal pattern.
• Reference ranges come from your laboratory’s report form; comparing a count with them is not a diagnosis. The conclusion belongs to the clinician.
• Cells and smear are schematic illustrations drawn by LabGuide, not micrographs; app screens are real (sample values).

LabGuide is a clinical-laboratory companion app for lab professionals and students (English, Russian, Uzbek). It is a learning and reference tool: it does not diagnose or interpret patient results. Works offline and without an account.
Get the app: [[LINK_APP_STORE]] · [[LINK_PLAY]]

Illustrative data — not patient results.
Educational use, not medical advice.
English synthetic narration (Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0); English subtitles.
Expert review pending: this content has not yet been reviewed by a laboratory specialist.
```

## 10. End screen / CTA suggestion

* YouTube end screen (last ~7–20 s): subscribe + the next video in the SAME language edition (`calibration`, `calculators`) + the playlist `[[LINK_PLAYLIST]]`. Place elements so they do not cover the end card's path pill or disclosure notices (check against the final scene).
* Description and pinned comment carry the store links (`[[LINK_APP_STORE]]`, `[[LINK_PLAY]]`); the video itself shows only the in-app path, no URL and no price.
* Instagram: link in bio (`[[LINK_BIO]]`); ask viewers to save/share, not to "download now".

## 11. Safe-content notes

* No patient data, names or real results anywhere. All numbers on screen are illustrative and labelled so.
* No third-party logo, brand name, stock footage or music. The only logo is the owner's app icon.
* Do not call the voice "natural", "professional" or "human": it is synthetic and nobody has listened to it yet.
* Do not call the content "approved", "verified", "certified" or "clinically validated": expert review is pending.
* No diagnosis, treatment, dosing or "normal range" statement. Reference ranges come from the user's laboratory.
* Do not answer individual medical questions in comments; point to the user's laboratory SOP, the reagent IFU and the clinician.
* No price, discount, product id or availability date in any text (docs/DECISIONS.md D-77/D-78: prices live in the stores).
* Check the platform's own disclosure setting for AI-generated / synthetic voice before posting (NEEDS_OWNER_CHECK: the rules change; the kit already states the voice is synthetic in the text).
* Audience: not made for kids. Category: Education. Comments: moderate; hide spam and requests for medical advice.
